:::{#exm-constant-wrt-vector}
#### A constant vector

Let $\vcoef = \tp{(\coef{1}, \coef{2})}$ and $\vx = \tp{(3, 5)}$,
so $x_1 = 3$ and $x_2 = 5$ do not depend on $\vcoef$.
Expanding $\deriv{\vcoef} \tp{\vx}$ into its matrix of scalar partial derivatives
(@def-vector-valued-derivative)
and evaluating each entry:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef} \tp{\vx}}_{2 \times 2}
&= \deriv{\vcoef} \sbmat{x_1 & x_2} \\
&= \sbmat{
\deriv{\coef{1}} x_1 & \deriv{\coef{1}} x_2 \\
\deriv{\coef{2}} x_1 & \deriv{\coef{2}} x_2
} \\
&= \sbmat{
\deriv{\coef{1}} 3 & \deriv{\coef{1}} 5 \\
\deriv{\coef{2}} 3 & \deriv{\coef{2}} 5
} \\
&= \sbmat{
0 & 0 \\
0 & 0
} \\
&= \underbrace{\matr{0}}_{2 \times 2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Every entry is the derivative of a constant, so $\deriv{\vcoef} \tp{\vx} = \underbrace{\matr{0}}_{2 \times 2}$
and $\vx$ is constant with respect to $\vcoef$ (@def-constant-wrt-vector).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-constant-wrt-vector}
#### A vector that is not constant

With the same $\vcoef$, let $\vx = \tp{(\coef{1}, 3)}$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef} \tp{\vx}}_{2 \times 2}
&= \sbmat{
\deriv{\coef{1}} \coef{1} & \deriv{\coef{1}} 3 \\
\deriv{\coef{2}} \coef{1} & \deriv{\coef{2}} 3
} \\
&= \sbmat{
1 & 0 \\
0 & 0
},
\end{aligned}
$$

which is not $\underbrace{\matr{0}}_{2 \times 2}$, so this $\vx$ is not constant with respect to $\vcoef$:
its first entry changes when $\coef{1}$ does.

:::
